prerequisites: It is essential that the student has passed the subjects Technical Thermodynamics and Fundamentals of Heat Transfer and Thermal Engineering.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of applied thermodynamics and heat transfer. Basic principles and their application to solving engineering problems.
Knows the functional and descriptive aspects of energy service installations in industry and buildings.
Relates the knowledge and skills acquired in previous subjects with their application in heat and cold production systems.
Knows how to select equipment and design heat and cold production, distribution, and accumulation installations.
Uses computer tools and handles different sources of information.
Knows how to apply economic criteria and thermal integration principles to heat and cold production systems.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert opinions, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle mandatory specifications, regulations, and standards.
Knows the regulations on safety, energy efficiency, and environmental protection in heat and cold production systems.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.

syllabus_topics: Calculation and analysis of thermal loads.
teaching_methods: Lectures: Expository sessions of theoretical and applied content. Basic concepts and fundamentals of thermal equipment and installations will be presented. Practical application cases of the studied systems will be explained.

Laboratory practices. The student becomes familiar with operating thermal systems and with experimental data collection and analysis. Applies the procedures specific to the subject and submits a results report.

Computer tool practices. The student learns to solve thermal engineering problems using computer tools. Applies subject-specific knowledge to problem-solving and practical cases and submits a results report.

assessment_methods.method: Participation in teaching activities and scheduled partial assessment tests (for continuous assessment)
Completion of practices, reports, and questionnaires associated with each session (for continuous assessment)
Global test on theoretical and practical contents of the subject (for first and second calls)

assessment_rules: To opt for continuous assessment, active participation in classes and completing tasks are essential, with partial tests (70%) and practices (30%) contributing to the grade. Students not opting for or failing continuous assessment can take a global exam (100%) in the first or second calls. Plagiarism or fraudulent copying results in a zero grade for the activity. Students must be able to demonstrate authorship of their work in an oral interview, otherwise, the grade for those activities will be zero.
